title: DR1 calls the sending party "Consignor"; the frontend calls it "Consignor or exporter" on the hub and as the picker's heading.

finding.frontend: One copy entry, `consignor: { title: 'Consignor or exporter' }` (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/copy/copy.en.js:20-21), supplies both the hub row title (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/controller.js:33-35,49) and the picker's h1 (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/party-picker.njk:8). fe-addresses-hub renders it as "Consignor or exporter" wrapping onto two lines in the summary-list key.
finding.prototype: DR1 names the same party "Consignor" everywhere a user sees it — the hub section heading, the picker h1 and the add link "Add a consignor" (app/data/consignment-address-sections.js:17-19, rendered at app/views/roles-and-addresses.html:49 and app/views/consignment-address-select.html:42). Only the internal section id keeps the longer form, `consignor-or-exporter`. Both sides give the same hint under it, "This is the sender of the consignment."
finding.difference: Change the user-facing label to "Consignor" in the addresses copy, which carries it to the hub row, the picker heading and the breadcrumb. This is a term change rather than a rewording: "or exporter" names a second legal role that DR1 does not put in front of the trader, and both sides describe the party identically in the hint, so nothing about who to enter changes. The route slug and the stored answer key stay as they are, matching DR1, which also kept the longer form internally. The validation message "Select a consignor from the list" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/copy/copy.en.js:23) already uses the shorter term, so the page contradicts itself today.
finding.falsifiedBy: "Consignor or exporter" appearing anywhere a DR1 user can see it, or a data-fields source that mandates the longer term for this label.
finding.correction: Verified, no change. The briefing's worry that DR1 might still say "Consignor or exporter" does not hold: the root section data reads `heading: 'Consignor'` at app/data/consignment-address-sections.js:17, and the rendered root hub confirms it — the section h2 is "Consignor" and the link is "Add a consignor", with only the section id keeping the longer `consignor-or-exporter` form, exactly as the finding says. The frontend side is observable too: the captured hub renders "Consignor or exporter" in the summary-list key and the captured picker renders it as the h1, the page title and the breadcrumb — one more place than the finding names, the browser title, which strengthens rather than weakens it. Frontend citations are exact: copy.en.js:21 is the title, :22 the hint and :23 the "Select a consignor from the list" error, so the self-contradiction the finding points at is real. This is not the DR1 parameterisation trap: the heading claim was read from the section data that drives all five roles, not from the one picture, which was shot in the place-of-origin role.
